title: Sphere eversion: obtain the witness from the immersion h-principle
intent: Prove the headline Smale sphere-eversion theorem — an existential ∃ f : ℝ → 𝕊² → E, smooth in both variables, f 0 = inclusion, f 1 = antipodal, every f t an immersion — by obtaining the witness f from the parametric immersion h-principle applied to a formal eversion, then discharging each conjunct against the bundle's projections and three endpoint lemmas.

parent.name: sphere_eversion
parent.statement:
theorem sphere_eversion :
    ∃ f : ℝ → 𝕊² → E,
      CMDiff ∞ ↿f ∧ (f 0 = fun x : 𝕊² ↦ (x : E)) ∧ (f 1 = fun x : 𝕊² ↦ -(x : E)) ∧
        ∀ t, Immersion (𝓡 2) 𝓘(ℝ, E) (f t) ∞ := by

children.name: immersionRel_satisfiesHPrincipleWith
children.statement:
theorem immersionRel_satisfiesHPrincipleWith
    [T2Space P] [SigmaCompactSpace P] [T2Space M] [SigmaCompactSpace M] [SigmaCompactSpace M']
    (h : finrank ℝ E < finrank ℝ E') (hC : IsClosed C) (hε_pos : ∀ x, 0 < ε x)
    (hε_cont : Continuous ε) : (immersionRel I M I' M').SatisfiesHPrincipleWith IP C ε
children.closed_by: (immersionRel_ample I I' h).satisfiesHPrincipleWith (immersionRel_open I I') hC hε_pos hε_cont

children.name: formalEversion_hol_near_zero_one
children.statement:
theorem formalEversion_hol_near_zero_one :
    ∀ᶠ s : ℝ × 𝕊² near {0, 1} ×ˢ univ, (formalEversion E ω s.1).toOneJetSec.IsHolonomicAt s.2
children.closed_by: filter_upwards [a neighbourhood (Iio (1/4) ∪ Ioi (3/4)) ×ˢ univ of {0,1} ×ˢ univ] then rcases the disjunction → formalEversionHolAtZero / formalEversionHolAtOne

children.name: formalEversion_zero
children.statement: theorem formalEversion_zero (x : 𝕊²) : (formalEversion E ω 0).bs x = x

children.name: formalEversion_one
children.statement: theorem formalEversion_one (x : 𝕊²) : (formalEversion E ω 1).bs x = -x

applicability.goal_shape: an existential goal ∃ f : D → E, P f whose body is a conjunction of properties of the witness (smoothness, endpoint values, a ∀-predicate over the parameter); the witness is produced by one named construction (here the parametric h-principle …SatisfiesHPrincipleWith … .bs applied to a formal solution), and each conjunct is a separate fact about the named witness
applicability.use_when: the witness arrives as a single bundle (a structure or an ∃ over several properties) and the goal's conjuncts match that bundle's projections; the remaining obligations are exactly the named lemmas you already hold about the candidate (endpoint values, holonomicity), so each closes independently
applicability.avoid_when: the goal needs a property the source lemma does not expose (you would have to re-open the bundle and re-derive it); the conjuncts must be proved jointly rather than one per child; or the witness is assembled interactively from several choices rather than obtained from a single lemma

claims.claim: The parent `sphere_eversion` (lines 307-340) closes using exactly four same-file lemmas — `immersionRel_satisfiesHPrincipleWith` (line 324) yields the witness `f`, `formalEversion_hol_near_zero_one` (line 327) is its holonomicity hypothesis, and `formalEversion_zero` (line 333) and `formalEversion_one` (line 336) close the two endpoint equalities — together with the projection fields `h₁` (smoothness) and `h₅` (injectivity) of the witness.
The file `SphereEversion/Global/Immersion.lean` contains no `sorry`, `admit`, `Admitted` or `axiom` token, and the project CI builds it (`lake build SphereEversion`) on every push and PR to `master`.

consequences: The ∃-goal becomes a `refine ⟨f, …⟩` with one obligation per conjunct, so a missing conjunct is a missing leaf rather than a partial proof. The witness's usable properties are only what the source lemma's bundle exposes (`h₁` smoothness, `h₂` agreement near `C`, `h₅` injectivity); here the immersion conjunct is reconstructed from `h₁` and `h₅` rather than taken as a single field. One field of the bundle is dropped with `-`, so if a later conjunct had needed it the `rcases` would have to be restructured. Definitional gaps between the witness and the goal's endpoint statement are bridged with `convert!` (lines 333, 336): the endpoint lemmas are stated for the reparametrized `formalEversion`, so they must match the `f 0 = …` goal up to definitional equality.
